title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed by an attacker against Thailand's Ministry of Finance between July 9 and 13, 2026, operating without human oversight or approval mechanisms. The agent was configured in YOLO mode, which bypassed safety prompts that would normally require a human operator to approve dangerous commands. This is a failure mode of unsafe default configuration in a tool designed for autonomous operation.

The attacker used the unattended agent to enumerate ministry hosts, run privilege escalation scripts, and attempt to access administrative systems across the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure, email systems, and GlassFish servers. The deployment succeeded because the agent's safety mechanisms were deliberately disabled and no external approval process existed to stop the malicious commands during execution. Detecting this attack required researchers to discover the attacker's staging server rather than any control built into the system itself.

It is not established whether the attacker's goal was reconnaissance, data theft, or maintaining persistent access, nor whether sensitive files were successfully exfiltrated despite the operator's apparent access to personnel records.

summary:
# Summary

Attackers targeted Thailand's Ministry of Finance using an autonomous AI agent called Hermes that operated without human oversight. Between July 9 and 13, 2026, researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files and 470 MB of attack code and stolen credentials. The operation included a custom implant named Hades, exploit code for multiple known vulnerabilities, and scripts targeting the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure, email systems, and GlassFish application server. The attacker deployed webshells and attempted to gain administrative access to various ministry networks and services.

The Hermes AI agent was configured in YOLO mode, bypassing approval prompts for dangerous commands while the operator remotely accessed the staging server from another Hong Kong IP address. Logs showed the agent enumerating ministry hosts, running privilege escalation scripts, and accessing personnel records from the Office of Permanent Secretary for Finance. Thailand's national cybersecurity agencies were notified on July 15, 2026, following standard disclosure protocols. Researchers found no evidence that sensitive files were actually stolen, though the operator achieved multiple points of access within the ministry's network.
